record.context_brief: embedded cmc disks with circular boundary
record.original_question: Is every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk in R^3 with circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.12 (4*). Is a compact embedded cmc disk of R3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, connected, embedded smooth surface with constant mean curvature (CMC), homeomorphic to the closed disk, and whose boundary $\partial \Sigma$ is a round circle in some plane of $\mathbb{R}^3$. Must $\Sigma$ be either a flat planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap bounded by that circle?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the only compact embedded CMC surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$ bounded by a circle are planar disks and spherical caps is widely cited as an open problem. Partial results are known: under additional hypotheses (e.g., the surface is a topological disk and stable, or is locally convex, or the mean curvature is sufficiently small relative to the radius), the conclusion has been established, but the general embedded-disk case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature surfaces with circular boundary in R^3
status_evidence.snippet: It is still unknown whether the spherical caps are the only examples of compact embedded surfaces with non-zero constant mean curvature bounded by a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that compact embedded CMC surfaces with circular boundary must be planar disks or spherical caps remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space
status_evidence.snippet: Whether spherical caps and discs are the only compact CMC surfaces bounded by a circle remains wide open.
status_evidence.claim: The disk-or-spherical-cap characterization for compact embedded CMC surfaces with circular boundary is an open problem.
